links.outcome: Sensitivity of LLM deferral to radiologist review for safety-critical or major missing-information requests
links.effect: Gemini 3.1 Pro had 100% sensitivity (38/38; 95% CI 90.7-100) for the 38 requests needing review, versus 94.7%-97.4% for the other pipelines.
links.quote: For the 38 requests with safety-critical issues or major missing information, Gemini 3.1 Pro achieved 100% sensitivity (38/38; 95% CI, 90.7-100), versus 94.7%-97.4% for other pipelines.

links.outcome: Unnecessary escalation of protocol-eligible requests to radiologists
links.effect: Unnecessary escalation ranged from 1.3% (5/371) to 34.0% (126/371) among protocol-eligible requests, lowest for reasoning-enabled models.
links.quote: Among 371 protocol-eligible requests, unnecessary escalation ranged from 1.3% (5/371) to 34.0% (126/371), remaining lowest for reasoning-enabled models.

links.outcome: Exact/equivalent protocol assignment of LLM pipelines compared with human protocolers on the same requests
links.effect: Human benchmark was 83.6% (95% CI 79.8-87.3). Exceeded by Gemini 3.1 Pro (+12.7 pp), Claude Sonnet 4.6 (+12.4), GPT-5.2 high (+11.6) and DeepSeek V3.2 reasoner (+8.6).
links.quote: The human benchmark achieved 83.6% (95% CI, 79.8-87.3) exact/equivalent assignment, exceeded by Gemini 3.1 Pro (+12.7 percentage points; 95% CI, 8.6-16.7), Claude Sonnet 4.6 (+12.4; 8.4-16.4), GPT-5.2 high (+11.6; 7.3-15.9), and DeepSeek V3.2 reasoner (+8.6; 4.3-12.9).

screen.practice: Guardrail-first deferral of incomplete or safety-critical requests to radiologists
screen.reason: The study evaluates a guardrail-first triage and escalation workflow that identifies incomplete or safety-critical radiology requests and defers them to human radiologists before automated LLM assignment.

primary.practice: guardrail triage and escalation to clinician review
